intro.p: Cognos is an encrypted AI chat application by Climacrux GmbH, St. Niklausenstrasse 96, 6047 Kastanienbaum, Switzerland.
We built Cognos for private, useful AI conversations. This policy explains what we collect, what we do with it, and what we deliberately do not do.
For privacy questions, contact us at support@cognos.io.

blocks.p: Cognos stores your chat history in an encrypted form.
That means:

ul: Stored chat history is encrypted so Cognos cannot read it from storage.
Live AI requests are processed in plaintext by our backend and the selected AI provider so the AI can answer.
We do not use your chats to train our own models.
We do not sell your personal data.
We do not share your data for advertising.
We require approved AI providers not to use Cognos chats for training.

blocks.p: This is not the same as full end-to-end encryption for the entire AI request path. Your stored history is protected, but when you send a message, that message has to be processed so the AI can respond.

sections.heading: Who is responsible for your data?

blocks.p: The controller is:

Climacrux GmbH
St. Niklausenstrasse 96
6047 Kastanienbaum
Switzerland
Email: support@cognos.io
We have not appointed a Data Protection Officer. We have not confirmed an EU or UK representative. This section may be updated after legal review.
Cognos is intended for users aged 16 or older, unless a different age applies under local law or after legal review.
Cognos is available worldwide, with a primary focus on Switzerland, the UK, Germany, France, Spain, Portugal, and Italy.
This policy currently covers the Cognos web app.
We collect the information needed to create, secure, and manage your account, such as:

ul: email address
password hash and authentication data
preferred language, theme, model, and privacy tier
avatar icon and colour

account settings and preferences
billing status and subscription references

Your chats may include:

ul: messages and prompts
AI responses
generated content
conversation titles
summaries and memory used to make conversations work better
supported file-derived context
personas and settings
redaction mappings

blocks.p: Stored chat history is encrypted at rest and decrypted client-side. Cognos does not store your Account Key on our servers.
During a live AI request, your message is processed in plaintext by Cognos backend systems and by the selected AI provider so the AI can generate a response.
You may upload supported files such as text, documents, PDFs, DOCX files, images, and code-like text.

Files are processed in the browser where possible for extraction, redaction, and encryption. They are encrypted before upload. File context may be sent to an AI provider when you use that file in a message.
We do not use uploaded files to train models.
We have not found current use of third-party OCR, transcription, malware scanning, or audio upload vendors. If this changes, this policy will be updated.
Payments are handled by Paddle.
Cognos does not store full payment card details. Paddle handles payment cards, tax, checkout, and invoices.
Cognos may store:

ul: Paddle customer and subscription IDs
billing status
invoice metadata
business name
VAT number
billing country
usage ledger data
limited card display details, such as brand, last four digits, or expiry, if provided by Paddle

blocks.p: Billing records are linked to your account, but not to your chat content.
We collect limited operational data to run, secure, and bill for the service, such as:

ul: IP address
user agent
timestamps
routes and request status
error information
model used
provider used
privacy tier
token counts
cost and latency metadata
billing identifiers

blocks.p: We do not intentionally log prompts, completions, message content, or encryption keys.
Approximate region may be inferred from your IP address by infrastructure or analytics providers. We do not collect precise location.
Cognos may use privacy-friendly product analytics, such as Plausible, to understand aggregate product usage.
If enabled, analytics are intended to be cookieless and not to include chat content, prompts, completions, or personal identifiers.
We do not use session replay, heatmaps, keystroke logging, screen recording, or advertising pixels.
We aim to respect Do Not Track and Global Privacy Control signals where applicable.
We process data to:

ul: provide the Cognos chat service
store encrypted chat history
route AI requests to selected models and providers
manage accounts, login, and MFA
process subscriptions and billing
provide support
secure the service
prevent abuse
maintain logs needed for operations and security
improve product reliability and usability
comply with legal, tax, and accounting obligations

blocks.p: Where GDPR-style rules apply, we rely on these legal bases:

ul: Contract: to provide Cognos, manage accounts, process subscriptions, and deliver AI responses.
Legitimate interests: to secure the service, prevent abuse, maintain essential logs, debug issues, and improve the product.
Legal obligation: to keep records required for tax, accounting, and legal compliance.
Consent: where required, for optional marketing or non-essential analytics.

blocks.p: Cognos lets users choose models. Model availability is gated by the user’s selected privacy tier, such as Switzerland-only, EU, or global options.
When you send a message, Cognos routes the request to the selected or eligible AI provider. That provider processes the prompt and response so the AI can answer.
We do not use your chats to train our own models.
We require approved AI providers not to use Cognos user data for training. Exact provider retention terms depend on our contracts and provider configuration.
Current or expected AI infrastructure includes:

ul: Infomaniak for Swiss-hosted models
Requesty as an EU gateway
the underlying model providers and hosts listed on our Subprocessors page

sections.heading: Subprocessors: who helps us run Cognos?

blocks.p: We use a small number of service providers to operate Cognos.
Some help us host the app, send emails, process payments, store encrypted backups, deliver the website, or provide AI responses. They may process personal data only for those purposes.
Important distinction:

ul: hosting and backup providers mainly process encrypted stored data and technical metadata
billing providers process payment and invoice data
email providers process email addresses and email content
AI providers process plaintext prompts and responses during live AI requests so the AI can answer

blocks.p: We do not let service providers sell Cognos user data or use it for advertising.

Some providers process only encrypted data or technical metadata. AI providers are different: they process live prompts and responses in plaintext so the AI can answer. Stored chat history remains encrypted so Cognos cannot read it from storage.
See our full, always-current subprocessor list — who each provider is, what they handle and where — on the Subprocessors page.

We require AI providers used with Cognos not to use Cognos user data for model training. Exact retention and routing terms depend on the provider and selected privacy tier. We use contractual safeguards where required, including data processing agreements and international transfer protections.
Cognos uses client-side encryption for stored chat data.
In practical terms:

ul: stored chat history is encrypted at rest
stored files and attachments are encrypted at rest
conversation titles, summaries, memory, personas, attachment manifests, artifacts, and redaction mappings are encrypted at rest
your Account Key is generated client-side and is not sent to Cognos servers
private keys are encrypted client-side before backup
conversation and file keys are wrapped or sealed for authorised users
live AI requests are processed in plaintext so the AI can answer

blocks.p: We also use security measures such as:

ul: TLS in transit
access controls
route authorisation
MFA support
rate limits
password lockout
hardened containers
firewall controls
backups
operational monitoring

blocks.p: Cognos staff should not be able to read stored chat content from the database. Staff access to production systems is restricted. Staff are not permitted to inspect plaintext live request flows except where strictly necessary and authorised for security or operational reasons.
We maintain incident-response procedures and restrict production access to authorised staff on a need-to-know basis, with access logged and reviewed.
We do not:

ul: sell your personal data
share your personal data for advertising
use your chats to train Cognos models
intentionally log prompts or AI completions
store full payment card details
use advertising pixels
use session replay, heatmaps, or keystroke logging
scan encrypted stored chat history for advertising or profiling

blocks.p: We use service providers to run Cognos. These vendors may process personal data only as needed to provide their services.
Current or planned service providers include:

ul: Hetzner, for app/backend hosting
Bunny.net, for CDN/DNS
BorgBase, for backups
Scaleway, for transactional email
Paddle, for payments, subscriptions, tax, and invoices

Plausible, if launched, for cookieless analytics

blocks.p: Some providers may process data outside Switzerland, the EU, or the EEA. Where required, we use appropriate safeguards such as data processing agreements and standard contractual clauses.
Cognos is operated by a Swiss company. Core app/backend hosting is currently on Hetzner infrastructure in Falkenstein, Germany. The frontend may be served through Hetzner and Bunny.net.
Depending on your selected privacy tier, AI provider, billing interactions, email delivery, CDN routing, support, or infrastructure services, your data may be processed in other countries.
Where required, we use contractual and legal safeguards for international transfers.

ul: language
theme
encrypted vault-session data
authentication state

blocks.p: Paddle may use its own cookies or storage during checkout.
If Plausible analytics is enabled, it is intended to be cookieless.
We do not currently use Google Analytics, PostHog, Meta Pixel, LinkedIn Ads, Sentry, or advertising cookies.
Cognos supports public chat sharing.
If you choose to make a chat public or share it through a public link, people with access to that link may be able to view the shared content. Only share conversations you are comfortable disclosing.
Cognos is designed for private questions, but you should avoid adding unnecessary sensitive personal data, confidential business data, health data, financial data, government IDs, or secrets.
Encryption and redaction reduce exposure, but they do not eliminate all risk. Live AI requests still require plaintext processing by Cognos backend systems and the selected AI provider.
We keep data only as long as needed for the purposes described in this policy.
Current retention approach:

ul: account data is kept while your account exists
chat data is kept until you delete it, it expires, or your account is deleted
deleted ordinary records are snapshotted for 30 days in a deleted-record table
key material and user attachment records are excluded from that 30-day deleted-record snapshot
removed user attachments are hard-deleted
financial records may be detached from your account and retained as required for accounting, tax, or legal purposes
backups follow a rotation of hourly, daily, weekly, monthly, and yearly snapshots
yearly backups may be kept for up to 10 years

blocks.p: Operational logs, support messages, and abuse or security records are kept only as long as needed for security, support, and legal obligations, then deleted or anonymised. Some billing records are kept for longer where accounting, tax, or legal rules require.
You can delete your account, subject to any steps needed to cancel an active paid plan first.

ul: conversations
messages
keys
projects, where applicable
personas
preferences
vault sessions

blocks.p: Financial records may be retained in detached form where required for legal, tax, accounting, refund, fraud-prevention, or compliance reasons.
Depending on where you live, you may have rights to:

ul: access your personal data
correct inaccurate data
delete your data
export your data
object to certain processing
restrict certain processing
withdraw consent
complain to a data protection authority

blocks.p: Cognos supports browser-side export for conversations and data. You can also delete conversations and manage account settings in the app.
To make a privacy request, email support@cognos.io.
We may need to verify your identity before fulfilling a request.

password reset
authentication and security messages
billing and subscription messages

If we receive a valid legal request for stored chat content, Cognos can only provide the encrypted content and metadata it has. Cognos cannot decrypt stored chat history from storage without the user’s Account Key and relevant keys.
Live AI request processing and metadata are different from encrypted stored history and may be subject to normal operational and legal processes.
Cognos is not intended for children under 16. If you believe a child has used Cognos in violation of this policy, contact us at support@cognos.io.

If changes are material, we will provide reasonable notice, such as through the app or by email.

security.title: Security
security.lead: A plain-language look at how Cognos is built, what we can and can’t see, and the limits we’re honest about.

intro.p: Cognos is an AI chat app built so that your saved conversations are kept in a form we can’t read. This page explains how that works, in plain language.
For the precise legal detail, see our Privacy Policy. For the providers behind Cognos, see Subprocessors.

blocks.p: Three parts work together every time you chat, and each is trusted with as little as possible.

ul: Your device holds the keys. Your chats are unlocked and read here, and nowhere else.
Our servers store your chats locked, pass your message to the AI, and lock the answer away again. They never keep a copy we can read.
The approved AI provider receives your message while it answers. We disable Provider retention and verify that setting before approval.

blocks.p: When a conversation is saved, it’s locked on your device before it reaches us — the messages, titles, summaries and any files. We store only the locked version, which we can’t read.
Only your key can open it again, and that happens on your device when you sign in.
You have two separate secrets, each with one job:

ul: Your password signs you in. Forget it and you can reset it by email — your chats stay safe, because the password doesn’t unlock them.

Your Account Key is the one that opens your chats. We never receive it or store it, so keep it somewhere safe. If you lose it, we can’t recover your chats for you — that’s the trade-off for keeping no copy we can read.

sections.heading: What we can and can’t see

blocks.p: We can see the details needed to run the service — your account and billing information, which model you used, and technical details like timestamps. While the AI is answering, your message is readable so the AI can work with it.
We can’t read your saved chats, titles, summaries, memory or files from storage. They stay locked with a key we don’t hold.

Before your message leaves your device, Cognos also hides common personal details — like emails, phone numbers, bank details and ID numbers — behind placeholders, so the AI works with placeholders instead of the real values.
Cognos is run by a Swiss company. The app and its stored data are hosted in Europe, and you choose whether AI models run in Switzerland only or across Europe.

We keep data only as long as we need it. Your chats stay until you delete them, they expire, or you close your account. Deleted items are held briefly in a recovery snapshot before they’re gone for good, and backups rotate on a regular schedule.
A short list of specialist providers helps us host the app, send emails, take payments and provide the AI. Most only ever handle data in a form we can’t read.
See the full list — who they are, what they handle and where — on the Subprocessors page.
The parts of Cognos that handle your data are open for inspection, so you can verify what we do rather than take our word for it.
Cognos hasn’t yet completed a formal independent security audit. We’ll say so here plainly when that changes.
We’re upfront about the limits:

ul: While the AI answers, your message has to be readable to our systems and the AI provider. This is the one moment it isn’t locked, and it’s never kept afterwards.
Hiding personal details is automatic but best-effort — it catches common things like emails and card numbers, not everything.
If someone reaches your device while it’s unlocked, they can see what you can see. Locking or signing out protects a device you’ve stepped away from.
If you lose your Account Key, your chats can’t be recovered.

blocks.p: Cognos is built to protect your saved chats if our storage or database is ever breached — not to hide your message from the AI while it’s answering.

blocks.p: Your conversation is saved and encrypted as you go. The list of chat titles is decrypted only on your device, so the sidebar loads quickly and privately.

note.body: Don't want it saved? Turn on a temporary conversation before you start.

figure.alt: A sent message and the assistant's reply in a conversation.
figure.caption: Your message and the reply — saved and encrypted automatically.

blocks.p: Above the message box you can choose a different model — some are faster, some are better at reasoning, some can search the web or make images.

choosing-a-model.metaDescription: Cognos offers many AI models. Pick one by name or filter by what you need — speed, reasoning, web search, or images.
choosing-a-model.title: Choosing a model
choosing-a-model.lead: Cognos offers many models. Pick one by name, or filter by what you need — speed, reasoning, web search, or images.

steps.title: Open the model picker
steps.body: Select the model name shown above the message box.

steps.title: Find one
steps.body: Browse Pinned, Recent and Recommended, search by name, or use the quick filters (Fast, Powerful, Reasoning, Web search, Image, Vision, and more).

steps.title: Select it
steps.body: Your choice sticks for new messages and follows you across devices.

figure.alt: The model picker showing pinned, recent and recommended models with quick filters.
figure.caption: The model picker, with quick filters along the top.

blocks.p: The model is the choice you make. The provider is the company that actually runs it and sees your message while it answers. Cognos records the provider on each answer — you can check it any time in the per-answer privacy details.

sections.heading: What a model can and can't do

ul: The picker only enables what a model actually supports — an image-only model can't hold a text chat, for example.
Web search is quietly skipped on models that can't do it, rather than blocking your message.
Your privacy tier limits which models you can use. Models above your tier appear greyed out so you can see what a higher tier would unlock.

privacy-tiers.metaDescription: Your privacy tier sets how far your messages may travel to be answered. It changes which models you can use — and nothing else.
privacy-tiers.title: Privacy tiers
privacy-tiers.lead: Your privacy tier sets the furthest your messages may travel to be answered. It changes which models you can use — and nothing else.

head: Tier
Your messages are handled…
rows: On Swiss soil only — the strictest option.
Within the EU/EEA, the UK and Switzerland.
In vetted data centres worldwide — unlocks every model.

steps.title: Open your account settings
steps.body: Go to Account and find the Data processing card.

steps.title: Pick a tier
steps.body: Select one of the three cards. It saves immediately and the model list updates.

figure.alt: The Data processing card with three privacy tier cards: Switzerland only, Europe, and Global.
figure.caption: The Data processing card on your Account page.

sections.heading: What it does and doesn't change

ul: Changes: which models you're allowed to use.
Doesn't change: how your chats are stored — they're always kept in a form we can't read, whatever tier you choose.

note.body: The tier is only about where a live answer is produced. Your saved conversations are encrypted the same way at every tier.

personas.metaDescription: A persona is a reusable instruction set that shapes how the AI replies — a tone, a role, a format. Use a built-in one or create your own.
personas.title: Personas
personas.lead: A persona is a reusable instruction set that shapes how the AI replies — a tone, a role, or a format. It's not a separate bot.

blocks.p: Cognos ships a set of built-in personas. Switch persona from the chip in the message box, or open the Personas page to browse them all.

steps.title: Open Personas and select New persona
steps.body: From the Personas page.

steps.title: Describe it
steps.body: Give it a name, a description, and the instructions the AI should follow. Add a colour and icon if you like.

steps.title: Optionally make it your default
steps.body: Turn on Use as default so it applies to new chats.

figure.alt: The Personas page showing pinned, recent and official personas in a grid.
figure.caption: Your personas, including the built-in "Official" ones.

ul: Your custom personas are private and encrypted.
Your default persona follows you across devices.
If a persona is deleted or can't be loaded, chat still works — it just falls back to no persona.
Personas are personal to your account; there's no shared persona.

reasoning.metaDescription: Some models can show their thinking before the final answer. See how to view reasoning and set how much effort a model spends.
reasoning.title: Reasoning
reasoning.lead: Some models can show their thinking before the final answer — and you control how much effort they spend.

blocks.p: On models that support it, each answer has a Show reasoning toggle. The thinking streams live, then tucks away once the answer arrives. It's encrypted like the rest of your message and never logged.

figure.alt: The reasoning effort control showing selectable levels.
figure.caption: Dial how much effort a capable model spends thinking.

blocks.p: The Reasoning effort control in the message box lets you dial a capable model from off up to high. More effort can take longer and cost more; the exact levels depend on the model.

note.body: Reasoning is a transparency aid, not proof — it can be incomplete or restate your prompt. Judge the answer, not the thinking.
Reasoning text isn't included when you export a conversation yet.

web-search.metaDescription: On some models, the AI can look things up on the web while answering and cite its sources. How to turn it on and what it costs.
web-search.title: Web search
web-search.lead: On some models, the AI can look things up on the web while it answers, and cite its sources.

blocks.p: Open the Tools menu in the message box and enable Web search. If the model you picked can't search, the option says so and is simply skipped.

figure.alt: The Tools menu with the Web search toggle.
figure.caption: Switch on Web search from the Tools menu.

ul: Your question may be sent to a search engine by the AI provider to find sources.
The results and citations are encrypted like the rest of your message, and shown inline as clickable sources.
Each search that runs adds a small flat fee on top of the usual cost — see plans & pricing.

note.body: Cognos doesn't run the search itself — the AI provider does. Web search works only on models that support it (currently certain Europe-hosted ones); your privacy tier doesn't change that.

temporary-conversations.metaDescription: A temporary conversation is never saved — messages stay in your browser until you close it. When to use one and how it differs from disappearing messages.
temporary-conversations.title: Temporary conversations
temporary-conversations.lead: A temporary conversation is never saved. Messages stay in your browser until you close it.

blocks.p: On a new, unsaved chat, turn on the Temporary chat toggle. Nothing is written as a saved Conversation — the messages live only in this browser.

figure.alt: The Temporary chat toggle on a new, unsaved conversation.
figure.caption: The Temporary chat toggle on a new conversation.

ul: Quick, throwaway questions you don't need to keep.
Working on a shared or public computer.

note.body: Temporary chats don't appear in your history or search, and aren't summarised.

disappearing-messages.metaDescription: Set messages to expire on a timer, or a whole conversation to auto-delete after a period of inactivity. Both are permanent.
disappearing-messages.title: Messages that delete themselves
disappearing-messages.lead: Set messages to expire on a timer, or a whole conversation to delete itself after a period of inactivity.

blocks.p: When you create a chat, you can set its messages to expire after 24 hours, 7 days, 90 days, or 180 days. Each message is deleted permanently once its timer runs out.

note.body: A file you attached stays in your Library even after the message that used it disappears.

figure.alt: The Disappearing messages dialog with expiry duration options.
figure.caption: Choosing how long messages last.

blocks.p: In a saved chat, open the ⋯ menu and choose Auto-delete to remove the whole conversation after a period of inactivity (Account default, Never, 7 days, or 30 days). Set the account-wide default under Account.
The countdown is based on the chat's last activity — tightening it later won't retroactively delete an old-but-recently-used chat.

note.body: Deleted content can't be recovered — not by you, not by Cognos. There's no backup and no undo.

redaction.metaTitle: Redaction: hiding sensitive details — Cognos Docs
redaction.metaDescription: Cognos can spot sensitive details in your message — like an IBAN or email — and hide them from the AI before you send. How it works and how to review it.
redaction.title: Redaction
redaction.lead: Cognos can spot sensitive details in your message — an IBAN, an email, a card number — and hide them before the AI ever sees them.

blocks.p: Detection runs in your browser before anything is sent. Each sensitive value is swapped for a placeholder like [[PII_IBAN_Q7K9M2]]. The AI provider and the saved message only ever see the placeholder — you still see the real value.
On your Account page, the PII redaction card offers Off, Simple (fast, the default) and Better (slower, catches more). Both run entirely on your device.

steps.title: Watch the summary
steps.body: The message box shows how many sensitive values it will hide.

steps.title: Check what's highlighted
steps.body: Select Show what will be redacted to see each detected value.

steps.title: Adjust if needed
steps.body: Deselect an item to send it as-is, or mark Never redact this for a value you always want left alone.

figure.alt: The message box showing detected sensitive values highlighted before sending.
figure.caption: Detected values are highlighted so you can review them before sending.

note.body: Detection leans towards caution and may miss something rather than mangle normal text. Always review the highlights before you send.

blocks.p: Select a placeholder in a sent message to open Personal information redacted, which compares what you see with what the model saw. Only someone holding the redaction key can reveal the real value — by default, that's just you.

note.body: When you share a conversation, a redacted-only link keeps values hidden; an include-sensitive link lets recipients reveal them. Choose carefully.

figure.alt: The Personal information redacted modal comparing what you see with what the model saw.
figure.caption: What you see versus what the model saw.

attachments.metaTitle: Attachments and your Library — Cognos Docs
attachments.metaDescription: Attach files to a message in Cognos. They're encrypted in your browser and stored in your personal Library to reuse across chats.
attachments.title: Attachments & your Library
attachments.lead: Attach files to a message. They're encrypted in your browser and kept in your personal Library, ready to reuse across chats.

steps.title: Open the Tools menu
steps.body: In the message box, open Tools → Attachments.

steps.title: Upload or reuse
steps.body: Choose Upload for a new file, or From library to reuse one. Unsupported file types are turned away rather than half-uploaded.

figure.alt: The message box with the paperclip button for attaching a file.
figure.caption: Attach a file from the message box.

blocks.p: Files belong to you, not to the chat — a conversation only points at a file. Manage them at File library: rename, download, or remove.

ul: Files are processed, redacted and encrypted in your browser before upload.
Remove a file and past messages show "File removed" rather than losing history.
Scanned PDFs get text extraction on your device (English, first version).
Size and per-account storage limits apply.

note.body: Attachments are always personal — even inside a shared Project, others can't open your files.

generating-documents.metaDescription: Turn any answer into a real Word, PDF, or Markdown file — built in your browser, never on Cognos servers.
generating-documents.title: Generating documents
generating-documents.lead: Turn any answer into a real Word, PDF, or Markdown file — built in your browser, never on our servers.

blocks.p: Use the download option on any assistant reply and pick a format — Word, PDF, or Markdown. The file is built on your device; the bytes never touch Cognos servers.

figure.alt: The Tools menu with the Create documents toggle.
figure.caption: Turn on Create documents in the Tools menu.

blocks.p: You can also ask the model to write one ("draft this as a PDF brief"). It appears as a document card you can download or save to your Library. Ask for changes and it re-emits the whole updated file.

ul: Generated files carry no personal author details — just "Cognos" — and dates are rounded to the day.
Generated spreadsheets can't "phone home" — network formulas are disabled and shown as plain text.
Turning off Create documents for a chat removes the feature there entirely.

generating-images.metaDescription: Describe an image and a capable model creates it. The result is encrypted like any other message.
generating-images.title: Generating images
generating-images.lead: Describe an image and a capable model will create it. The result is encrypted like any other message.

steps.title: Enable image generation
steps.body: Turn on Generate image in the message box.

steps.title: Describe what you want
steps.body: Write your prompt and send.

figure.alt: The Tools menu with the Generate image toggle.
figure.caption: Turn on Generate image in the Tools menu.

ul: The model may reply with a clarifying question instead of an image — that's normal, not an error.
Select regenerate to make an alternative version alongside the original.
A chat containing images exports as a .zip (text-only chats export as .json).
Image generation is billed per image — see plans & pricing.

projects.metaDescription: A Project groups related conversations in one place. Personal projects are just for you; Organisation projects are shared with your team.
projects.title: Projects
projects.lead: A Project groups related conversations in one place. Personal projects are just for you; Organisation projects are shared with a team.

steps.title: Open Projects
steps.body: Go to Projects and select New project.

steps.title: Set it up
steps.body: Give it a name, and optionally an icon, colour, and a default model.

figure.alt: The Projects page listing projects.
figure.caption: The Projects page.

ul: Personal project — just you. It can't be shared with other people.
Organisation project — shared with members of your Organisation, each with a role of Viewer, Editor, or Admin.

blocks.p: From a chat's ⋯ menu, choose Move to project or Remove from project. You need to be an Admin of both the chat and the project.

note.body: Attachments stay personal even inside a shared project — members can't open each other's files.

bookmarks.metaDescription: Highlight any part of a message and save it. Your bookmarks are private to you, even in a shared conversation.
bookmarks.title: Bookmarks
bookmarks.lead: Highlight any part of a message and save it. Your bookmarks are private to you — even in a shared chat.

blocks.p: Select some text in a message, then choose Save to bookmarks. Cognos keeps the quote plus a little surrounding context so it can find the spot again.
Open Bookmarks to see them all, and select one to jump back to the exact spot in its conversation.

figure.alt: The Bookmarks page listing saved highlights.
figure.caption: Your bookmarks, browsable in one place.

ul: Bookmarks are encrypted and readable only by you — even if the chat is shared, others never see them.
If a message has changed too much to find the exact quote, the bookmark still lists — it just won't highlight a spot.

searching-conversations.metaDescription: Search your chats from the sidebar. It runs entirely on your device — nothing you search for ever leaves your browser.
searching-conversations.title: Searching your chats
searching-conversations.lead: Search your conversations from the sidebar. It all runs on your device — nothing you search for leaves your browser.

blocks.p: Use the Search box in the sidebar (three characters or more). It matches conversation titles instantly and searches recent message content too, with title matches ranked first.

figure.alt: The sidebar search box with matching conversations.
figure.caption: Searching your conversations from the sidebar.

blocks.p: The search index is built and used only on your device — nothing you type is sent to us or logged. The index is cleared whenever you lock, log out, or switch accounts.

note.body: This is different from web search, which asks the AI to look things up online.

importing-conversations.metaDescription: Bring your ChatGPT or Claude conversations into Cognos. Your export is read and encrypted in your browser — the raw file isn't uploaded.
importing-conversations.title: Importing conversations
importing-conversations.lead: Bring your ChatGPT or Claude conversations into Cognos. Your export is read and encrypted in your browser.

steps.title: Open the import page
steps.body: Go to Import.

steps.title: Pick your source
steps.body: Choose ChatGPT or Claude and follow the on-screen steps to select the export file you downloaded from them.

steps.title: Review, then confirm
steps.body: Check the preview counts so you know exactly what will come across, then confirm.

figure.alt: The import page with source options for ChatGPT and Claude.
figure.caption: The import page.

ul: Reading and encrypting happen in your browser — the raw export isn't uploaded to us.
Up to 10,000 messages per conversation.
Branching threads are split into clearly labelled separate conversations, never guessed or merged.
Re-importing the same file is safe — it won't create duplicates.
Imported chats arrive as standalone conversations; move them into a Project afterwards if you like.

note.body: Unsupported content (PDFs, images, tool records) is left out by design — the preview counts show what will and won't come across.

sharing-conversations.metaDescription: Publish a read-only link to a conversation that anyone can open — with or without the sensitive details revealed.
sharing-conversations.title: Sharing a conversation
sharing-conversations.lead: Publish a read-only link to a conversation that anyone can open — with or without the sensitive details revealed.

steps.title: Open the conversation and select Share
steps.body: The Share button is in the chat header.

steps.title: Choose what to include
steps.body: Decide whether to keep sensitive values hidden or let recipients reveal them (see below).

steps.title: Copy the link
steps.body: Send it however you like. Select Stop sharing any time to revoke it.

figure.alt: The Share conversation dialog with a public link and a toggle for including sensitive values.
figure.caption: The Share dialog, with the option to include or hide sensitive values.

head: Mode
What recipients see
rows: Sensitive values stay hidden as placeholders.
Recipients can reveal the real values without signing in.

note.body: Include-sensitive means anyone with the link can see the real redacted values. Use redacted-only unless you truly mean to share them.

figure.alt: A public, read-only view of a shared conversation with sensitive values hidden.
figure.caption: A shared link in redacted-only mode — sensitive values stay hidden.

sections.heading: How a shared link stays private

blocks.p: The key that unlocks a shared conversation lives inside the link itself (after the #), which browsers never send to our servers — so we can't read a shared conversation from our logs. Revoking a share breaks the link immediately, without affecting the conversation.

note.body: A public share is read-only and grants no membership. Collaborating with named people happens through Organisation projects.

multi-factor-authentication.metaDescription: Add a second step to sign-in: a 6-digit code from an authenticator app. It protects your login — your Account Key still protects your data.
multi-factor-authentication.title: Two-factor authentication
multi-factor-authentication.lead: Add a second step to signing in — a 6-digit code from an authenticator app. It protects your login, not your data.

steps.title: Open Security & keys
steps.body: Go to Security & keys and select Enable two-factor authentication.

steps.title: Confirm your password
steps.body: Then scan the QR code with an authenticator app, or type the setup key by hand.

steps.title: Enter a code to confirm
steps.body: Type the 6-digit code from the app and select Verify and enable.

steps.title: Save your recovery codes
steps.body: Store the recovery codes you're shown — they're your way back in if you lose the app.

figure.alt: The two-factor setup screen showing a QR code and a field to enter a 6-digit code.
figure.caption: Scan the QR code, then confirm with a 6-digit code.

blocks.p: After your password, you'll enter the current 6-digit code. Ticking Remember this device for 30 days skips the code on that device for a while.

ul: Authenticator app only — Cognos doesn't send codes by email.
Trusted devices are cleared when you log out, disable two-factor, regenerate recovery codes, or change your password.
Two-factor guards your login. Your data is still unlocked by your Account Key.

note.body: There's no two-factor reset. If you lose both your authenticator app and all your recovery codes, you won't be able to sign in — so keep those codes safe.

recovery-codes.metaDescription: Recovery codes are one-time backup codes that get you in if you lose your authenticator app. How to save, use, and regenerate them.
recovery-codes.title: Recovery codes
recovery-codes.lead: Recovery codes are one-time backup codes that get you in if you lose your authenticator app.

blocks.p: When you enable two-factor authentication, Cognos shows 10 recovery codes once. Copy or download them and store them safely — they can't be shown again.

figure.alt: The two-factor authentication card where recovery codes are set up.
figure.caption: Recovery codes are set up alongside two-factor authentication.

blocks.p: On the code screen at sign-in, choose Use a recovery code instead and enter one. Each code works exactly once.
From Security & keys you can regenerate the set (it needs your password and a current code). This cancels the old codes and signs out trusted devices.

note.body: Lose your authenticator app and all your recovery codes and there's no way back in — there's no support reset. This protects login only; your data is governed by your Account Key.

resetting-your-password.metaDescription: Forgot your password? Reset it by email. This never affects your encrypted chats or your Account Key.
resetting-your-password.title: Resetting your password
resetting-your-password.lead: Forgot your password? Reset it by email. This never affects your encrypted chats or your Account Key.

steps.title: Open the reset page
steps.body: Go to Reset your password and enter your email.

steps.title: Open the emailed link
steps.body: It takes you to a page to choose a new password.

steps.title: Choose a new password
steps.body: Set it and you're done.

figure.alt: The reset your password page with an email field.
figure.caption: Request a reset link by email.

note.title: Your chats are untouched
note.body: Your password only signs you in. Resetting it never re-encrypts or touches your conversations, and it doesn't change your Account Key.

blocks.p: If you have two-factor authentication on, a password reset doesn't bypass it — you'll still need your code.

your-privacy.metaDescription: A plain-language summary of what Cognos can and can't see, and the controls that keep your conversations yours.
your-privacy.title: Your privacy
your-privacy.lead: A plain-language summary of what Cognos can and can't see — and the controls that keep it that way.

blocks.p: The content of your saved conversations, attachments, bookmarks and memory is kept in a form we can't read. It's unlocked only on your device, with your Account Key.

ul: Metadata needed to run the service — when a message was saved, and what a request cost.
The AI provider that answered each message (recorded on the answer).

blocks.p: The AI provider does see your message while it answers — that's how any AI assistant works. Privacy tiers control where that happens.
The Security button on a conversation shows, for each answer, which model and provider handled it and where — so you can verify it matches your settings.

figure.alt: A modal comparing what the account holder sees with what the model saw.
figure.caption: You always see your real values; the model only saw placeholders.

cards.title: Privacy tiers
cards.body: Limit where messages may be handled.

cards.title: Memory
cards.body: Decide what the AI remembers — privately, or shared in a project.

note.body: Full detail lives on the Security overview and Privacy Policy.

account-memory.metaDescription: Memory lets the AI remember facts and preferences you choose — across your chats, or within a project. It's opt-in and encrypted.
account-memory.title: Memory
account-memory.lead: Memory lets the AI remember facts and preferences you choose — across your chats, or within a project.

blocks.p: You can store facts, preferences and instructions for the AI to reuse. Memory can be account-level (private to you, used across your chats) or project-level (shared with the people in that Project).
Turn personal memory on or off and edit entries at Memory. It's encrypted, and redaction is applied before memory is sent with a request.

note.body: Memory is opt-in — Cognos doesn't build a picture of you unless you add one. Editing or deleting an entry only affects future messages.

figure.alt: The Memory settings page.
figure.caption: Manage what the AI remembers on the Memory page.

sessions-and-logout.metaTitle: Sessions and logging out — Cognos Docs
sessions-and-logout.metaDescription: Logging out of Cognos ends your session everywhere and clears your unlocked data. What it does, and how to sign out other devices.
sessions-and-logout.title: Sessions & logging out
sessions-and-logout.lead: Logging out ends your session everywhere and clears your unlocked data. Here's exactly what it does.

blocks.p: The Log out button in the sidebar signs out every device at once, clears the convenience unlock cache, and forgets any devices you'd told to remember your two-factor code.
To end other sessions without logging yourself out here, use Sign out other devices on Security & keys.

figure.alt: The Sign out other devices card on the Security & keys page.
figure.caption: Sign other devices out without logging yourself out here.

blocks.p: To get back in you'll need your password, then your Account Key to unlock again.

note.body: Just want to hide your data on this device without signing out? Use Lock instead.

deleting-your-account.metaDescription: Permanently delete your Cognos account and all your personal data. What to do first, what's removed, and what's kept.
deleting-your-account.title: Deleting your account
deleting-your-account.lead: You can permanently delete your account and all your personal data. This can't be undone.

ul: Cancel any paid subscription first.
If you own an Organisation, transfer it or dissolve it first.

steps.title: Open the Danger zone
steps.body: It's at the bottom of your Account page.

steps.title: Confirm it's you
steps.body: Type DELETE, enter your password, and (if two-factor is on) a current code.

steps.title: Confirm
steps.body: Your personal data is removed.

figure.alt: The Danger zone with the delete account controls.
figure.caption: The Danger zone on your Account page.

ul: Removed: your conversations, messages, personas, bookmarks, library files, memory, redaction mappings and two-factor records.
Kept: Organisation-owned projects you created stay with the Organisation; some financial records may be retained (detached from you) for legal reasons.

note.body: There's also Delete all chats, which clears your conversations but keeps your account. Losing your Account Key isn't a route to deletion — you can still sign in and delete.
Deletion is permanent — there's no recovery.

plans-and-pricing.metaDescription: Start with free trial credit, then choose Pay-As-You-Go or Unlimited. How Cognos prices usage, and where to pick a plan.
plans-and-pricing.title: Plans & pricing
plans-and-pricing.lead: Start with free trial credit, then choose Pay-As-You-Go or Unlimited. Payments run through Paddle.

head: Plan
How it works
rows: A free starting balance. When it's used up, your account is read-only until you pick a plan.
You pay for what you use, with a CHF 15 monthly minimum.
A flat CHF 150 a month (or CHF 1'500 a year) under fair use.

blocks.p: On Pay-As-You-Go, your cost for a message is the AI provider's cost plus a 22% margin, converted to Swiss francs. Each web search that runs adds a small flat fee.
Pick or switch a plan from the pricing page or your billing settings.

figure.alt: The pricing page showing Pay-As-You-Go and Unlimited plan cards.
figure.caption: The Pay-As-You-Go and Unlimited plans.

note.body: Your trial chats stay fully readable even after the credit runs out — you just can't send new messages until you pick a plan.

trial-credit.metaDescription: Every new Cognos account starts with a small amount of free credit so you can try it before choosing a plan.
trial-credit.title: Trial credit
trial-credit.lead: Every new account starts with a small amount of free credit, so you can try Cognos before choosing a plan.

blocks.p: A small starting balance lands on your account automatically at signup. You can spend it once your email is verified, and the amount left is shown in the sidebar.

figure.alt: The trial credit card in the sidebar showing the remaining balance.
figure.caption: Your trial balance, shown in the sidebar.

blocks.p: Your account becomes read-only: your existing chats stay fully readable, but you'll need a plan to send new messages.

note.body: There's no Organisation trial — Organisation work is billed from the start.

managing-your-subscription.metaDescription: View usage, download invoices, switch plans, or cancel — all from your billing settings. Payments are handled by Paddle.
managing-your-subscription.title: Managing your subscription
managing-your-subscription.lead: View usage, download invoices, switch plans, or cancel — all from your billing settings.

blocks.p: Plan & billing shows your current plan, usage this period, payment method, and invoice history with PDF downloads. Payments and the payment portal are handled by Paddle.

figure.alt: The Plan & billing page with the current plan and invoices.
figure.caption: The Plan & billing page.

blocks.p: Switch between Pay-As-You-Go and Unlimited, or cancel, from the same page.

ul: A quick check before each message makes sure you can cover it, so you're never charged for something you can't afford.
That check uses a worst-case estimate — the real charge is usually smaller, and the difference stays in your favour.

note.body: Cancel any subscription before deleting your account.

organisations-overview.metaDescription: An Organisation is a billing and admin boundary for a team. It pays for shared work and keeps conversation content private from admins.
organisations-overview.title: Organisations
organisations-overview.lead: An Organisation is a billing and admin boundary for a team. It pays for shared work — and keeps content private, even from admins.

blocks.p: An Organisation groups people through memberships, owns shared Projects, and pays one pooled bill. There are three roles:

ul: Owner — billing and dissolving the Organisation.
Admin — members, seats, policy, and the usage dashboard.
Member — works in the projects they're added to.

note.body: Organisations are available to selected design partners today.

figure.alt: The Team settings page for an Organisation.
figure.caption: The Team page, where Organisations manage members.

steps.title: Create an invite
steps.body: In Settings → Team, create an invite and copy the link (it's shown once).

steps.title: Send it your way
steps.body: Share the link however you like — Cognos doesn't email it for you.

steps.title: They accept, you add them
steps.body: The invitee signs up if needed, then opens the link to join. An Admin then adds them to specific projects.

note.body: Invite links are single-use and expire after 14 days. Lost a link? Revoke it and issue a new one.

sections.heading: What admins can and can't see

note.title: Metadata only — never content
note.body: Admins see usage metadata: seats, per-member cost, and model mix. They never see message content, conversation titles, or memory.

seats-and-billing.metaDescription: Organisations pay one bill: CHF 15 per seat per month, with a three-seat (CHF 45) minimum. How pooled usage and overage work.
seats-and-billing.title: Seats & billing
seats-and-billing.lead: Organisations pay one bill: CHF 15 per seat per month, with a three-seat (CHF 45) minimum.

blocks.p: Every active membership takes one seat, billed at CHF 15 per seat per month. An Organisation is always billed for at least three seats (CHF 45 a month), even with fewer active people.

figure.alt: The Team settings page showing members and seats.
figure.caption: Members and seats on the Team page.

blocks.p: All members' work in Organisation projects pools into one bill. Usage above the combined seat floor is billed as a single overage line at the end of the cycle. Organisation work always bills the Organisation — never a member's personal balance.

ul: There's no Organisation trial — billing starts from day one.
Removing a seat mid-cycle isn't refunded; the count drops at the next cycle, and never below three.
If Organisation billing lapses, its projects go read-only for everyone until it's resolved.

organisation-projects.metaDescription: Organisation projects are shared workspaces owned by the organisation. Work in them is billed to the organisation.
organisation-projects.title: Organisation projects
organisation-projects.lead: Organisation projects are shared workspaces owned by the Organisation. Work in them is billed to the Organisation.

blocks.p: Only active members can be added to an Organisation project, each as a Viewer, Editor, or Admin. Organisation Admins are Admins on every Organisation project automatically. The mechanics are the same as personal Projects.

figure.alt: The Projects page listing projects.
figure.caption: Projects — personal or Organisation-owned.

blocks.p: Every message in an Organisation project bills the Organisation, not the person typing. If Organisation billing lapses, its projects become read-only for everyone until it's fixed.
Offboarding cuts a person's access first, then a key rotation locks them out of future messages. Their personal account and personal data are untouched.

note.body: Attachments are personal even here — members can't open each other's files, and shared file libraries aren't available yet.

branches.metaDescription: Change a question or ask for another answer — Cognos keeps every version so you can switch between them any time.
branches.title: Editing, regenerating & versions
branches.lead: Change a question or ask for another answer, and Cognos keeps every version — switch between them whenever you like.

steps.title: Hover the message you sent
steps.body: Its actions appear.

steps.title: Choose Edit message
steps.body: Change the wording.

steps.title: Send it again
steps.body: Your original question and its answer stay put — the edit starts a new version alongside them.

blocks.p: Ask the model for another take and the new answer sits alongside the first, rather than replacing it.
When a turn has more than one version, a small ‹ 1/2 › control appears. Use the arrows to move between them — the rest of the conversation follows whichever version you're viewing.

note.body: Switching only changes what you see and what the AI uses for context. Nothing is deleted — every version stays in your history.

figure.alt: A conversation turn showing a version switcher with previous and next arrows.
figure.caption: The version switcher appears when a turn has more than one version.

exporting-your-data.metaDescription: Your conversations are yours. Download them any time in a readable format — no lock-in, and the export happens on your device.
exporting-your-data.title: Export your data
exporting-your-data.lead: Your conversations are yours. Download them any time, in a readable format — no lock-in.

blocks.p: On your Account page, the Your data section lets you export and download your conversations. They're decrypted in your browser and saved straight to your device.

figure.alt: The Your data card on the Account page with export and download options.
figure.caption: The Your data section on your Account page.

ul: Your conversations in a portable file you can keep or move elsewhere (a .zip when a chat includes images).
Any single answer, on demand, as a Word, PDF, or Markdown file — see generating documents.
The export runs on your device — nothing extra is sent to us to produce it.

note.body: The model's reasoning (its “thinking”) isn't included in exports yet — only your messages and the answers.

blocks.p: Because you can export any time — and neither your password nor your plan locks your data — you're never stuck. Even if your plan lapses, your existing chats stay readable; you just can't send new messages until you pick a plan.

note.body: Exporting keeps your data; deleting your account removes it. They're separate choices.
